paragraphs.en: Goffin's cockatoos, {native} to Australasia, are a kind of small {parrot} that has a white body with hints of yellow and {orange} .They {mimic} sounds and {dance} to music, which often {amuses} their owners.The cockatoos have been shown to have similar shape-recognition abilities to a human two-year-old.Though not known to use tools in the {wild} , the {birds} have proved {skillful} at tool use while being kept in {cages} .In a recent experiment, cockatoos were presented with a box with a {nut} inside it.The clear front of the box had a“ {keyhole} ”in a {geometric} shape, and the birds were given five differently {shaped} “keys” to choose from. {Inserting} the {correct} “key” would let out the nut.
paragraphs.cn: 戈芬凤头鹦鹉 <u> 原产 </u> 于澳大拉西亚，是一种小型 <u> 鹦鹉 </u> ，身体呈白色，有少量黄色和 <u> 橙色 </u> 羽毛点缀。它们会 <u> 模仿 </u> 声音，还能随着音乐 <u> 起舞 </u> ，常常 <u> 逗乐 </u> 它们的主人。经验证，凤头鹦鹉的形状识别能力与人类两岁的儿童相近。尽管人们不知道这种 <u> 鸟 </u> 在 <u> 野外 </u> 会使用工具，但它们被关在 <u> 笼子 </u> 里时却已证明自己在使用工具方面很 <u> 熟练 </u> 。在最近的一项实验中，研究人员给凤头鹦鹉展示了一个装有 <u> 坚果 </u> 的盒子。盒子透明的正面有一个 <u> 几何 </u> 形状的“ <u> 钥匙孔 </u> ”，研究人员给这些鸟儿五把不同 <u> 形状 </u> 的“钥匙”供它们选择。 <u> 插入正确的 </u> “钥匙”就能让坚果掉出来。

paragraphs.en: In humans, babies can put a round shape in a round hole from around one year of age.They are quite {gifted} in their {vision} and can make {subtle} {discriminations} between different shapes.But it will be another year before they are able to do the same with less symmetrical (（对称的）) shapes.This ability to recognize that a shape will need to be turned in a specific direction to fit within the {boundary} of the puzzle is called an “allocentric frame of reference”.It is linked to understanding {geometry} .Developing this skill helps in activities like reading a {map} or navigating new environments.In the experiment, Goffin's cockatoos were able to select the right tool for the job, in most cases, by visual {recognition} alone.Where trial-and-error was used, the cockatoos did better than {monkeys} in similar tests.This {indicates} that Goffin's cockatoos do indeed {possess} an allocentric frame of reference when moving {objects} in space, {implying} that these birds have cognitive abilities {comparable} to those of two-year-old babies.The {comparison} has {astonished} researchers who had underestimated the {extent} to which animal intelligence can develop.
paragraphs.cn: 对于人类来说，婴儿从一岁左右起就能把圆形放入圆孔中。他们在 <u> 视觉 </u> 方面极具 <u> 天赋 </u> ，能够对不同的形状做出 <u> 细微的区分 </u> 。但要再过一年，他们才能对不太对称的形状做到同样的操作。这种认识到一个形状需要朝特定方向转动才能与拼图的 <u> 边界 </u> 相契合的能力被称为“异我中心参照系”。它与理解 <u> 几何图形 </u> 相关。培养这种能力有助于看 <u> 地图 </u> 或在新环境中辨别方向等活动。在实验中，戈芬凤头鹦鹉在大多数情况下仅通过视觉 <u> 识别 </u> 就能选取合适的工具。在使用“试错法”的情况下，凤头鹦鹉在类似测试中的表现要优于 <u> 猴子 </u> 。这 <u> 表明 </u> ，在空间中移动 <u> 物体 </u> 时，戈芬凤头鹦鹉确实 <u> 拥有 </u> 异我中心参照系，这 <u> 意味着 </u> ，这种鸟类具有与两岁婴儿 <u> 相当 </u> 的认知能力。这一 <u> 对比 </u> 结果让研究人员感到 <u> 震惊 </u> ，因为他们此前低估了动物智力发展的 <u> 程度 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: The next step, according to the researchers, is to try and work out whether the cockatoos rely entirely on visual {clues} , or also use a sense of touch in making their shape {selections} .Findings of future studies should represent significant {progress} in the field of animal cognition and may lead to {innovations} in how we appreciate animal minds.
paragraphs.cn: 据研究人员所述，下一步是尝试弄清楚凤头鹦鹉在 <u> 选择 </u> 形状时是完全依赖视觉 <u> 线索 </u> ，还是也会运用触觉。未来研究的结果有望在动物认知领域取得重大 <u> 进展 </u> ，并且可能会促使我们以 <u> 全新方式 </u> 去理解动物的思维。 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
